correctness.rationale: For fixed anchor i the blockwise top-coordinate selections are independent and finite-block truncation tends monotonically to A_i(x). Heredity holds using the same anchor, including when a subset no longer meets that block. Anchor 1 takes at least half the mass in every block and all the first block; lattice domination gives the upper bound. Equal mass on each of the first k blocks, uniform within each, gives A_i=1/k+(k-i)/(k2^i) on i<=k and zero thereafter, and maximum (k+1)/(2k); a coordinate vector attains the upper ratio. Thus the completion is ℓ1. For nonzero x, A_i(x) is bounded by the ℓ1 tail from i and hence an anchor attains the norm. Fix it when x_m tends coordinatewise to x with converging norms. Its contribution from j>J is at least 2^-i times the ℓ1 tail there. Subtract the continuous finite-head contribution and take limsup to bound the sequence tails by 2^i times the omitted contribution of x, tending to zero with J. The x=0 case follows from norm equivalence. A bounded sequence admits a coordinatewise convergent subsequence and Fatou gives an ℓ1 limit; finite equinorming supplies the upper bound on the limiting norms and the supremum of finite coordinate seminorms gives lower semicontinuity. Kadec then gives norm convergence. Conversely, a finite norm net and finite selections approximating its members' norms yield equinorming by Lipschitz continuity. In Definition 7, use uniform weights on D=B_i and on a whole B_j beyond any cutoff. Capturing more than half of D forces anchor i; the remote capture then has fraction at most 2^-i, which can be made smaller than any positive γ. This works throughout the source's admissible 0<γ<=1; γ>1 is outside that definition and impossible as a coverage fraction. Theorems 12–13 supply the compactness implication via Theorem 9, not in isolation.
residual_risks: The argument for positive γ does not assert failure at γ=0 or classify the range λ>=1/2.

evidence: Theorems 12–13 require a positive secondary fraction retained exactly or in a limit (0,c), c>0. The uniform-block test rules out those hypotheses. Theorem 14 concerns failure at secondary fraction zero, a different condition.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither the difference-set criterion without an additional implication, nor ℓ1-equivalence alone, yields the one-set statement. The explicit uniform tail estimate under the frozen norm's attained anchor supplies the missing implication.

value.rationale: The prior sparse example shows that the sufficient directedness condition is not necessary in general. The frozen construction answers the more constrained question in a familiar hereditary ℓ1 setting, where the source also has a contrasting ℓ1-equivalent negative example. The sharp comparison and fixed-anchor control explain why one-set equinorming succeeds in this realization despite the failure of positive uniform capture. The point is not the numerical constant alone or a repeat of the qualitative existence claim.
residual_risks: A concrete separation in one geometry; not a general criterion for hereditary families or equivalent ℓ1 norms.
